content.title: Sporting CP 5-0 Bodø/Glimt: 5-3 agg, UCL R16
content.text: Sporting CP produced a commanding UEFA Champions League Round of 16 second leg at Estádio José Alvalade, beating Bodø/Glimt 5-0 after extra time to win 5-3 on aggregate. The hosts erased a 3-0 first-leg deficit with a relentless performance built on pressure, width and set-piece quality. How the comeback unfolded Gonçalo Inácio started it on 34 minutes, heading in a Francisco Trincão cross. After the break, Pedro Gonçalves doubled the lead from close range following a clever pass by Luis Javier Suárez. Suárez then converted a 78th-minute penalty to level the tie on aggregate before extra time beckoned. Extra time, extra goals Sporting kept pushing. In the 92nd minute, Maximiliano Araújo arrived at the back post to turn in Trincão’s low delivery for 4-0 on the night. With the visitors stretched, Daniel Bragança stepped up to win the ball high and slipped in Rafael Nel, who finished on 120+1 to complete a famous 5-0 and the overall turnaround. Numbers that back it up Sporting dominated possession at 66% and fired 38 shots, 14 on target, to Bodø/Glimt’s 9 and 3. The xG read 3.35 to 0.54. Corners were 16 to 4 and big chances 9 to 0, a clean sweep that mirrors the scoreline. Nikita Haikin made 9 saves for the visitors, which kept the margin in check for long stretches. Standout performers on Sofascore – Gonçalo Inácio earned a Sofascore Rating of 9.5, pairing a goal with 126 passes and firm defending. – Maximiliano Araújo scored and created three big chances for a 9.0. – Francisco Trincão delivered two assists, 10 crosses and 4 key passes for an 8.0. – Luis Javier Suárez posted 1 goal and 1 assist with 3 shots on target for an 8.2. – Rui Silva registered a 7.6, including 1.35 goals prevented, as Sporting kept a clean sheet. What it means A relentless second leg sends Sporting CP into the Champions League quarter-finals. Bodø/Glimt’s brave first-leg work was undone by sustained pressure in Lisbon, especially from wide areas and set plays.
